title: Binary Search Trees
text: A binary search tree is a rooted binary tree data structure with key-value pairs where the left subtree contains keys smaller than the parent node and the right subtree contains keys greater.

title: Red-Black Self-Balancing Trees
text: Red-black trees are balanced binary search trees that maintain logarithmic search, insertion, and deletion time complexities through node coloring and rotations.

title: Hash Tables and Collision Resolution
text: Hash tables implement associative arrays using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets, resolving collisions via chaining or open addressing.

title: Hierarchical Navigable Small World
text: HNSW is a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search algorithm constructing a multi-layered geometric hierarchy of proximity graphs with logarithmic search complexity.

title: Dijkstra Shortest Path Algorithm
text: Dijkstra algorithm computes single-source shortest paths on weighted directed graphs with non-negative edge weights using a priority queue min-heap in O((V + E) log V) time.

title: A* Heuristic Graph Search
text: A* is an informed search algorithm that finds the shortest path between nodes using an admissible heuristic function f(n) = g(n) + h(n) to prioritize graph traversal.

title: Transformer Attention Mechanisms
text: The Transformer architecture relies on multi-head self-attention mechanisms to model bidirectional contextual relationships across sequence tokens without recurrent neural units.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
text: CNNs apply spatial convolutions and pooling filters over multi-dimensional grid structures, serving as the foundation for modern computer vision and image classification.

title: Gradient Descent and Backpropagation
text: Gradient descent minimizes differentiable loss functions by taking iterative steps proportional to the negative gradient computed via the chain rule in backpropagation.

title: Relational Databases and ACID
text: Relational database management systems utilize SQL queries, relational algebra, B-trees, and write-ahead logs to guarantee Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

title: B-Trees and Disk Storage
text: B-trees and B+ trees are self-balancing search trees optimized for storage systems that read and write large blocks of data, minimizing costly secondary disk I/O.

title: Distributed Consensus and Raft
text: The Raft consensus algorithm provides fault-tolerant state machine replication in distributed systems through leader election, log replication, and commit safety.

title: MapReduce Distributed Computation
text: MapReduce is a programming model and framework for processing massive datasets across clusters using parallel map operations followed by shuffle and reduce stages.

title: Operating System Virtual Memory
text: Virtual memory provides hardware memory abstraction through paging, translation lookaside buffers, and page tables, mapping virtual addresses to physical RAM frames.

title: CPU Scheduling and Context Switching
text: Operating system schedulers manage CPU core allocation among concurrent threads using algorithms like round robin, multi-level feedback queues, and fair share scheduling.

title: Public-Key Cryptography and RSA
text: RSA cryptography enables secure digital communication and digital signatures using modular exponentiation and the computational hardness of factoring large prime products.

title: TLS Protocol and Network Handshakes
text: Transport Layer Security provides encrypted network communication across the Internet using symmetric session keys negotiated via asymmetric cryptographic handshakes.

title: Vector Search and High-Dimensional Similarity
text: Vector search engines perform semantic search over dense embeddings generated by deep learning models, enabling content-based retrieval across unstructured corpora.

title: TF-IDF Term Weighting
text: Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency is a statistical numerical statistic reflecting how important a word is to a document within a large collection or corpus.

title: Inverted Index for Full-Text Search
text: Inverted index data structures map unique terms to posting lists containing document identifiers and term frequencies, powering fast keyword search engines.

title: QuickSort and Divide-and-Conquer
text: Quicksort is an efficient divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm that selects a pivot element and partitions array elements into sub-arrays of smaller and greater values.

title: MergeSort and Guaranteed O(N log N)
text: Merge sort is a stable comparison-based divide-and-conquer algorithm that recursively splits sequences in half and merges sorted halves with guaranteed O(N log N) runtime.

title: Graph Traversals BFS and DFS
text: Breadth-first search traverses graphs level by level using a queue, while depth-first search explores branches to their maximum depth using recursion or an explicit stack.

title: Dynamic Programming and Memoization
text: Dynamic programming solves complex optimization problems by decomposing them into overlapping subproblems and caching intermediate solutions via memoization or tabulation.

title: Skip Lists Probabilistic Data Structure
text: Skip lists are probabilistic data structures that augment linked lists with multiple layers of forward pointers, providing logarithmic search similar to balanced trees.
